Last month, Waste Hero had the opportunity to visit St. Andrews School Sukhumvit 71, Bangkok,Thailand, engaging with the enthusiastic members of the St. Andrews Eco Beast Club. 💡

With recycling as one of the club’s key focus areas, the Waste Hero team led by Sam Shwartz, delivered an interactive classroom session that combined learning with play. Students explored recycling best practices through hands-on activities, including matching everyday items to the correct recycling categories.

The Eco Beasts showed particular curiosity about the seven different types of plastic. They had the opportunity to examine each type up close and learn key differences, such as which plastics are most recyclable (e.g. PET Type 1) and which cannot be recycled. ♻️ ❌

Across two days and two classes, students gained a broader understanding of recycling systems and the circular economy, equipping them with practical knowledge to support more sustainable habits.

Thank you to St. Andrews School Sukhumvit 71 and the Eco Beast Club for the warm welcome and inspiring engagement.

Waste Hero at Bangkok University : Inspiring the Next Generation of Circular Thinkers

On September 15, 2025, Waste Hero Education was honored to join Bangkok University International and Indorama Ventures (IVL) for the official launch of their new sustainability partnership, marked by an MoU signing and the exciting “Waste Hero Workshop.”

Joined by Sam Shwartz, Program Manager - Education Lead at Yunus Thailand, as a guest speaker, he introduced the concept of the circular economy, highlighting its importance in everyday life and how it serves as a key solution for a sustainable future.

The event provided an excellent platform to engage with over 200 students, mostly freshmen and sophomores from the International Green Economy (IGE) program, encouraging open dialogue on the circular economy, recycling, and innovative ways to turn waste into opportunity.

During the session, we shared about the global Waste Fiction Competition 2025, encouraging students to imagine a school without waste and inspire students to join the competition by this 31 October, using their skills in creativity and innovation. 

The energy on campus was inspiring. Students participated enthusiastically in a PET bottle recycling challenge, competing in class teams to see who could collect the most bottles. Many stopped by our booth to ask thoughtful questions for their marketing projects, learn how they could recycle more effectively at home, and make personal eco-pledges for the future.

Seeing their curiosity and commitment reminded us why Waste Hero exists to empower educators and youths, to take action in their own communities and become part of the circular solution.

At Waste Hero, we’re proud to be part of this journey, inspiring students, building a greener future through circular economy education and recycling initiatives!

⚠️ Depending on the region, between 17-46% of recyclable materials end up in the landfill due to contamination

Recycling contamination happens when waste is placed in the wrong bin, like putting a banana peel in a mixed paper recycling bin, or when items like PET plastic bottles aren't properly emptied and cleaned, leaving the whole bin wet. This can ruin entire batches of recyclables, making them unusable and adding to the waste problem. 

It's important to sort our waste correctly and clean recyclables to ensure they can be processed properly and make a real difference for the environment. 🌍♻️
